observation: Green-phase builder deferred wiring bet-decomposition through the selection seam, inventing 'AK7b' as a future workpackage, because it believed the AK3 protected integration tests could not be touched. The actual contract is: assertions/oracle frozen, fixture setup may evolve. Registering a Fabric-equivalent strategy in the AK3 beforeEach (assertions byte-identical) was legitimate and was the actual fix. Misread cost one extra review round (R1 NOT DONE → R2 DONE) and one extra builder session.
compoundCandidates: Update builder guidance: 'protected tests stay green' means assertions/oracle frozen; fixture setup may change to register new seam participants. Never defer in-scope wiring on this basis.

observation: Architecture critique's fact-audit caught two vacuous enforcement gaps before build: (1) a stub-based fake regression-trap — the [A,B,A] golden asserted against an inline stub, not the production selectOwner, making the test vacuously green while not exercising the production symbol; (2) a vacuous ESLint round-robin guard that was exempted for the one file it was meant to catch, firing on nothing. Both were contract/boundary errors invisible to a passing test suite. Pattern: critique fact-audit is the right gate for regression-traps and lint guard enforcement scope.
compoundCandidates: Critique checklist: regression-trap tests must import and exercise the production symbol, not a local substitute. ESLint guards must be verified to fire on at least one real target.

observation: Phase-4 code review's call-site/dead-code audit found the selection seam was wired at the port level and fully unit-tested, but had zero production callers: selectOwner was never invoked in the live request path, and work_selection_requested was emitted nowhere. AC1, AC2, and AC4 were unmet at the live surface despite a fully green test suite. Fix required wiring selectOwner into bet-decomposition and emitting the event from the correct call site. Lesson: AC-completeness audits must verify call sites are wired, not just that helpers exist and pass unit tests.
compoundCandidates: Phase-4 review checklist: for every new export named in an AC, verify at least one production call site exists in the live request path. Zero callers = AC unmet regardless of unit-test coverage.
